title: Reduce tail latency for paginated dashboard endpoints using probabilistic shard-sampling and micro-index summaries
creator: Anika Patel
description: Background: Certain multi-tenant dashboard endpoints (usage breakdown, per-route cost, recent errors) show heavy tail latency during large time-window queries with deep pagination. Root causes: uneven shard hotness, full-shard scans for top-K with stable cursors, and repeated deserialization of large materialized rows. Proposal: implement a light-weight per-shard micro-index (summary row per time bucket + top-N sample) and a probabilistic shard-sampling phase for the first N pages. This reduces work on hot shards, enables early answers for shallow pagination, and allows fallthrough to full queries only when needed.
acceptance_criteria: P50 latency for first page of /dashboard/usage reduces by >= 30% on 95th-percentile tenant traffic
P95 tail latency for pages 1-3 reduces by >= 40% across production traces gathered during load window
No data regressions: query result top-K must have >= 98% overlap with baseline for page size <= 50 in sampled mode
Feature gated behind rollout flag and canaryed to internal tenants (10%) before wider rollout
Automated integration test that validates sampling fallthrough returns identical results for <= 2% of test cases (expected).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch with micro-index and sampling behind feature flag
2) Unit + integration tests in CI, synthetic load harness run in staging
3) Canary deploy to internal tenants (10%) with observability dashboards for overlap, latency, errors
4) Expand to 50% tenants if no regressions for 48 hours, then to 100% after 7 days
5) Post-ship: enable adaptive sampling thresholds from runtime metrics
rollback_plan: Disable feature flag immediately if error rate or mismatch > 2%
If latency regressions occur, revert to previous commit and restore micro-index snapshot from pre-deploy backup
Run a targeted reindex of affected time buckets if corruption suspected
measuring_success: Alert: >1% increase in 5xx for dashboard endpoints after canary
Cost: token and VM CPU reduction for query pipeline measured weekly
notes: Tradeoffs: sampling reduces immediate accuracy for deep, low-cardinality queries but significantly reduces wasted work on heavy shards.
Decision: micro-index will store aggregated counts and a deterministic top-20 hashed sample per time-bucket to allow cheap approximate ranking.
Implementation detail: micro-index rows are stored as compact protobufs in the existing materialized-store with a TTL of 90 days; reindex job will populate historical buckets lazily.
Compatibility: fallthrough path will run full scan and merge; sampling never hides items — only delays them until fallthrough if mismatch threshold exceeded.
Performance precaution: sampling stage must be CPU-bound but avoid extra network hops; design favors co-located reads in shard leader.
